description_en: Dhantila Vārāhī, one of the eight Mātrikās (Aṣṭamātṛkās) of Lalitpur, occupies an important place in the city’s sacred geography. As part of a protective network of Mātrikā shrines established around Lalitpur, her shrine was placed in the northwestern sector. Local tradition holds that the goddess was originally the guardian deity of Nandigrāma (Hā̃ḍīgāũ) and that she was swept downstream by the Bagmatī River to her present location. Because she is enshrined in Dhantila Ṭola, she is known locally as Dhantila Vārāhī. Her name is often Sanskritized to “Dhanvantari Vārāhī” due to its phonetic resemblance to Dhanvantari, the deity of Āyurveda, and because she is believed to possess healing powers. Devotees worship her to improve their fate (daśā) or to seek recovery from illnesses that medicine cannot cure.According to genealogical chronicles (vaṃśāvalī), during the reign of King Śivasimha Malla in Nepal Saṃvat 709 (1589 CE), the goddess announced to the people of Nandigrāma that she was about to be carried away by the Bagmatī River. When they ignored her warning, the nāgas at Chobhar increased the river’s current, and the goddess was swept downstream. She eventually came to rest at a point where the current could not carry her further, and this spot became her new abode. Before departing, she cursed the inhabitants of Nandigrāma and settled on the banks of the Bagmatī in Lalitpur (Yogī Naraharinātha VS 2013, p. 73). TheNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(2016, 19.3.1–2) attributes this event to the reign of King Hariharasiṃha Malla. Initially, only apīṭha(altar) was installed at the site; the temple was constructed later, though no historical record survives indicating the date or patron of its construction.The present temple is a single-storeyed, north-facing structure surmounted by a metalkalaśa-shaped finial. The roof is covered with brass sheets, and metal leaves hang from the finial down to the roof edges. A woodentoraṇacarved with the image of Vārāhī is set above the sanctum doorway. Inside, the goddess is represented by a four-armed metal image mounted on a buffalo. In her right hands she holds a sword and displays thevitarka mudrā; in her left she holds a shield and a vessel. Originally, an unshaped stone served as her aniconic representation; this stone was later buried beneath the floor, and the current cast-metal image was installed above it. Several unshaped stones placed on either side of the goddess are venerated as other Mātrikās. The sanctum walls are lined with marble, and in front of the temple is a platform in the shape of the letter “T.”The oldest extant inscription at the site dates to Nepal Saṃvat 906 (1785 CE). It records that Matsyendrasimha Bhāro of Dattalācheṃ (Dhālācheṃ) Ṭol built aphalca(resting pavilion) in the name of Lakṣmīramaṇa Upādhyāya and his three wives Dhanthakuṃ, Lakṣmī, and Pālulakṣmī. He endowed three ropanis of land as guthi to fund annual worship of Dāmodara (Gaṇeśa), Sarasvatī, and Lakṣmī on 3rd of bright fortnight of Kārtika, followed byśrāddharituals. Brahmins, Brahmaṇīs, Jyotiṣīs, and Karmācāryas were to be invited, and any surplus funds were to be spent on feasts for the guthi caretakers. These caretakers included Bhajusimha Bhāro (Olā Ṭola), Gajendrasimha Bhāro (Kobahā Ṭola), Vīranarasimha Bhāro (Sātiglā/Saugaḷ Ṭola), and Cikiti Bhāro (Dattalācheṃ Ṭola). Thephalcano longer survives, though asataḥ(platform) remains. Matsyendrasimha Bhāro was also responsible for repairing the Bālakumāri Temple (LAL2000) after earthquake damage in Nepal Saṃvat 928 (1808 CE) (cf.LAL2000_I_20200922_08).In 1918 CE (VS 1975), Jita Govinda Amātya of Daubāhā Ṭola and his sons Kīrtigovinda and Pūrṇagovinda constructed aghāṭaon the Bagmatī River at Dhantila. Following the theft of the original image of Vārāhī, a new cast-metal image was installed in 2003 CE (VS 2059) by Kṛṣṇanātha Māske and his wife Śakuntalā Māske. They also tiled the sanctum floor, applied copper sheeting (ilāṃ), and gilded (jalapa) thetoraṇa. After the 2015 CE (VS 2072) earthquake caused structural damage, Balrām K.C. of Kopuṇḍol sponsored the temple’s restoration in 2019 CE (VS 2076) in memory of his late parents Kālugaṇḍe and Kāñchī K.C. and his late wife Bhagavatī K.C.No full-time priest is appointed for the shrine. Instead, members of theDyaḥpālaḥcommunity perform priestly duties on a rotational monthly basis among 65 households. They clean the temple each morning and conduct daily worship, supported financially by devotees’ offerings. The Jyāpu community of Kumbheśvar organizes the annual Dhantila Vārāhījātrā. On the evening of Piśāca Caturdaśī, the metal image of the goddess is brought from the guthi house in a covered palanquin (ḍhakī) to the temple, worshipped in the sanctum for several hours, and then carried back to Kumbheśvar in procession. Additionally, several Jyāpu and Khaḍgī families in Lalitpur revere Dhantila Vārāhī as theirkuladevatā(lineage deity) and visit the shrine annually for ancestral worship on 6th of bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha (sithinakhaḥ) and 14th of dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa (Bālā Caturdaśī).
description_ne: नन्दीग्रामबाट बगाएर ल्याएको भन्ने जनविश्वास रहेको धंतिल वाराहीलाई ललितपुरमा रहेका अष्टमातृकामध्ये एक मानिन्छ ।ललितपुर शहरको सुरक्षार्थ विभिन्न स्थानमा मातृकाका पीठहरू स्थापना गरिएका थिए । ती मातृकामध्ये ललितपुरको उत्तर-पश्चिम दिशामा वाराहीको स्थापना गरिएको थियो । धंतिल टोलमा स्थापना गरिएको हुनाले स्थानीयहरू धंतिल वाराही भन्ने गर्छन् । आयुर्वेदका देवता धन्वन्तरीसँग 'धंतिल' शब्दको ध्वनि साम्यता रहेको र धंतिल वाराहीले पनि रोग निको पार्ने विश्वास गरिएकोले 'धंतिल वाराही'लाई संस्कृतकरण गरी 'धन्वन्तरी वाराही' पनि भन्ने गरिएको छ । कसैको दशा बिग्रिएको छ भने यी देवीको पूजा गरेपछि दशा सुधार हुन्छ भन्ने जनविश्वास रहेको छ । कसैलाई रोग लागेर औषधी गर्दा पनि निको नभएमा यी देवीको पूजा गर्नाले निको हुने विश्वासले पूजा गर्न आउनेहरू पनि छन् ।धंतिल वाराहीको पीठलाई एकतले मन्दिरको स्वरूप दिइएको छ । उत्तराभिमुख गरी बनाइएको मन्दिरमा कलशाकार धातुको गजूर राखिएको छ । मन्दिरको छानामा पित्तलको पाता राखिएको छ । गजूरदेखि छानासम्म पुग्ने गरी धातुको पताः झुण्ड्याइएको छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि वाराही अङ्कित काष्ठतोरण राखिएको छ । चार हात भएकी वाराहीले दायाँ दुई हातमा खड्ग र वितर्क मुद्रा धारण गरेकी छिन् भने बायाँ दुई हातले ढाल र पात्र धारण गरेकी छिन् । गर्भगृहभित्र आकृतिविहीन ढुङ्गालाई वाराही मानी स्थापना गरिएको थियो । पछि त्यस ढुङ्गालाई भुइँमा नै गाडी त्यसमाथि ढलोटको वाराहीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । राँगोमाथि चढेकी चार हात भएकी वाराहीले दायाँ दुई हातमा खड्ग र पात्र धारण गरेकी छिन् भने बायाँ दुई हातले ढाल र वितर्क मुद्रा धारण गरेकी छिन् । वाराहीको दायाँबायाँ आकृतिविहीन केही ढुङ्गाहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । ती ढुङ्गाहरूलाई पनि मातृकादेवीको रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ । गर्भगृहको भित्तामा मार्बल टाँसिएको छ । मन्दिरअगाडि अंग्रेजी वर्णमालाको 'T' आकारको सतः बनाइएको छ ।धंतिल वाराहीको स्थापनाबारे कुनै अभिलेख पाइएको छैन । वंशावलीअनुसार यी देवी नन्दीग्राम (हाँडीगाउँ) की रक्षक देवी थिइन् । त्यहाँका मानिसहरूले देवीलाई पूजा नगरी बेवास्ता गरेका थिए । राजा शिवसिंह मल्लको राज्यकालमा नेसं ७०९ (सन् १५८९) मा देवीले नन्दीग्रामवासीलाई सम्बोधन गरी मलाई बागमतीले बगाउन लाग्यो भन्दाखेरि पनि मानिसहरूले वास्ता गरेनन् । त्यसको चारदिनपछि चोभारका नागले पानीको बेग बढाई देवीलाई बगाइदियो । बगाउँदै लग्दा बागमती दोभान नाघेपछि अड्किएर बगाउन सकेन । जुन ठाउँमा देवी अड्किएको थियो त्यसै ठाउँमा देवीलाई स्थापना गरिएको थियो । देवीले नन्दीग्रामवासीलाई श्राप दिई ललितपुरको बागमती नदी किनारमा नै विराजमान भएकी थिइन् (Yogī Naraharinātha VS 2013, p. 73) ।Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(2016, 19.3.1-2) मा राजा हरिहरसिंह मल्लको पालामा वाराहीलाई बगाएर ल्याइएको घटना दिइएको छ । पहिले स्थापना गर्दा पीठ मात्र भएपनि पछि मन्दिर बनाइएको थियो । मन्दिर कसले र कहिले निर्माण गरेका थिए भन्ने कुराको जानकारी दिने ऐतिहासिक सामग्री पाइएको छैन । मन्दिरमा प्राप्त सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं ९०६ (सन् १७८५) को शिलापत्र हो । उक्त शिलापत्रमा ललितपुर, दत्तलाछेँ (धालाछेँ) टोलका मत्स्येन्द्रसिंहले फल्चा निर्माण गरेको कुरा लेखिएको छ । उनले लक्ष्मीरमण उपाध्याय र उनका तीन श्रीमतीहरू धनथकुं, लक्ष्मी र पालुलक्ष्मीको नाममा उक्त फल्चा बनाएका थिए । उनले फल्चाको लागि तीन रोपनी खेत पनि गुठी राखिदिएका थिए । उक्त खेतको आयस्ताले प्रत्येक वर्ष कार्तिक शुक्ल ३ मा दामोदर (गणेश), सरस्वती, लक्ष्मीको पूजा गरी श्राद्ध गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । श्राद्धमा ब्राह्मण, ब्राह्मणी, जोशी, कर्माचार्यलाई अनिवार्य रूपले बोलाउनुपर्ने नियम बनाइएको थियो । सबै पूजाहरू समाप्त भएपछि बाँकी रहेको रकमले गुठीको चिन्ता गर्नेहरूलाई भ्वज खुवाउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । गुठीको चिन्ता गर्नेहरू भनी ओला टोलका भाजुसिंह भारो, कोबाहाः टोलका गजेन्द्रसिंह भारो, सातिग्ल (सौगल) टोलका वीरनरसिंह भारो र दत्तलाछेँ टोलका चिकिति भारोको नाम उल्लेख गरिएको छ । धंतिल वाराही देवस्थल परिसरमा एउटा सतः मात्र देखिन्छ, कुनै फल्चा देखिँदैन । त्यसैले मत्स्येन्द्रसिंहले निर्माण गरेको फल्चाको अस्तित्व समाप्त भएको हुनसक्छ । यी उनै मच्छिन्द्रसिंह भारो थिए जसले नेसं ९२८ (सन् १८०८) मा भूकम्पले क्षति पुगेको बालकुमारी मन्दिर (LAL2000) को जीर्णोद्धार गरिदिएका थिए (cf.LAL2000_I_20200922_08) । विसं १९७५ (सन् १९१८) मा ललितपुरको दौबाहाः टोलमा बस्ने जितगोविन्द अमात्यले छोराहरू कीर्तिगोविन्द र पूर्णगोविन्द अमात्यसँग मिलेर बागमती प्रवाह भइरहेको धंतिल भन्ने ठाउँमा घाट निर्माण गरिदिएका थिए । वाराहीको पुरानो मूर्ति चोरी भएकोले विसं २०५९ (सन् २००३) मा कृष्णनाथ मास्के र उनकी श्रीमती शकुन्तला मास्केले ढलोटको नयाँ बनाएर स्थापना गर्नुको साथै गर्भगृहभित्र टायल छाप्ने, तामाको इलां चढाउने, तोरणमा सुनको जलप लगाउने काम गरेका थिए । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा केही क्षति पुगेकोले विसं २०७६ (सन् २०१९) मा कोपण्डोल निवासी बलराम के.सी.ले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिदिएका थिए । उनले दिवंगत बुबा कालुगण्डे के.सी., दिवंगत आमा कान्छी के.सी. र दिवंगत श्रीमती भगवती के.सी.को सम्झनामा उक्त जीर्णोद्धार कार्य गरेका थिए ।यस देवस्थलमा पुजारी भनी छुट्टै व्यवस्था गरिएको छैन । द्यःपाःलाःले नै पुजारीको काम गरिरहेका छन् । उनीहरूले बिहान सबेरै मन्दिरको सरसफाइ गरी नित्यपूजा गर्छन् । उनीहरूका ६५ घरले एक-एक महिनाको पालो मिलाएर देवस्थलमा पुजारी र द्यःपाःलाःको काम गरिरहेका छन् । भक्तजनले चढाउने भेटी नै उनीहरूको आन्दानीको स्रोत रहेको छ । कुम्भेश्वरमा बस्ने ज्यापुहरूले धंतिल वाराहीको जात्रा चलाइरहेका छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष पिशाच चतुर्दशीको साँझ ती ज्यापुहरूले आफ्नो गुठीघरमा राखिएको धंतिल वाराहीको धातुको मूर्तिलाई ढकीमा राखेर जात्रा गरी धंतिल वाराहीको देवस्थलमा ल्याउँछन् । देवस्थलको गर्भगृहभित्र केही घण्टा राखेर पूजा गरिसकेपछि पुनः ढकीमा राखेर जात्रा गरी कुम्भेश्वर फिर्ता लग्ने गर्छन् । ललितपुरमा रहेका केही ज्यापु र खड्गी समुदायका मानिसहरूले धंतिल वाराहीलाई आफ्नो कुलदेवता मानेर पूजा गर्छन् । उनीहरू ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल ६ (सिथिनखः) र मंसीर कृष्ण १४ (बालाचतुर्दशी) को दिन पारेर कुलदेवताको पूजा गर्न आउँछन् ।

historical_events.event_description: Matsyendrasimha of Dattalācheṃ (Dhālācheṃ) Ṭola, Lalitpur, constructed aphalcain the name of Lakṣmīramaṇa Upādhyāya and his three wives Dhanthakuṃ, Lakṣmī, and Pālulakṣmī. He also endowed threeropanīsof land as guthi for its upkeep. The income generated from this land was designated to fund annual worship of Dāmodara (Gaṇeśa), Sarasvatī, and Lakṣmī on 3rd of bright fortnight of Kārtika, followed byśrāddharituals. It was mandated that Brahmins, Brāhmaṇīs, Jyotiśīs, and Karmācāryas be invited to these ceremonies. Any remaining funds after the rituals were to be used to provide a feast for the guthi caretakers. The inscription lists these caretakers as Bhajusimha Bhāro of Olā Ṭola, Gajendrasimha Bhāro of Kobahā Ṭola, Vīranarasimha Bhāro of Sātiglā (Saugaḷ) Ṭola, and Cikiti Bhāro of Dattalācheṃ Ṭola. At present, only asataḥ(raised platform) remains within the Dhantila Vārāhī shrine precinct; nophalcasurvives, indicating that the pavilion built by Matsyendrasiṃha has likely disappeared over time.
Jita Govinda Amātya of Daubāhā Ṭola, Lalitpur, together with his sons Kīrtigovinda and Pūrṇagovinda Amātya, constructed aghāṭa(riverbank platform) at Dhantila on the Bagmatī River.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a new statue of Vārāhī
historical_events.event_description: After the original image of Vārāhī housed in the sanctum was stolen, Kṛṣṇanātha Māske and his wife Śakuntalā Māske of Bālīphala Ṭola, Lalitpur, commissioned and installed a new cast-metal image of the goddess. On this occasion, they also tiled the sanctum floor, added copper sheeting (ilāṃ), applied gilding (jalapa) to the toraṇa, and installed an iron fence around the temple for security.
Rāma Byañjankāra, Cirīmāyā Byañjankāra, and other individuals jointly installed an oil-lamp balustrade in front of the temple.
Hīrāmāna Byañjankāra and Nānīthakuṃ Byañjankāra jointly installed a bell (LAL2960-008) on the eastern side of the temple.
Rāmamāyā and Harimāyā jointly installed another bell (LAL2960-009) on the eastern side of the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of a marble inscription commemorating offerings
historical_events.event_description: In place of the stolen image of Vārāhī, Kṛṣṇanātha Māske and his wife Śakuntalā Māske installed a new cast-metal image. On this occasion, they also tiled the sanctum floor, applied copper sheeting (ilāṃ), and gilded thetoraṇa(jalapa). To commemorate these works, a marble inscription was placed inside the sanctum.
Dhanamayaju Mā of Śaṅkhamūla organized apīṭha pūjā(altar worship) with prayers for the welfare and liberation of living beings.
Indrakumāra Śreṣṭha and his wife Mīrā Śreṣṭha of Jwāgal jointly installed a bell (LAL2960-006) to the east of the entrance gate leading into the shrine precinct.
Indrakumāra Śreṣṭha and his wife Mīrā Śreṣṭha of Jwāgal also jointly installed another bell (LAL2960-007) to the east of the entrance gate of the shrine precinct.
In memory of the late Gajanārāyaṇa Śāhī and the late Harkhamāyā Śāhī, Kṛṣṇabahādura Śāhī, Jvālādevī Śāhī, and others installed a Dharmadhātujinālaya caitya in the temple courtyard.

After the temple sustained some damage in the 2015 CE (VS 2072) earthquake, Balrām K.C. of Kopaṇḍola undertook its restoration in memory of his late father Kālugaṇḍe K.C., his late mother Kāñchī K.C., and his late wife Bhagavatī K.C.
Bīrena Khaḍgī, Rośanī Khaḍgī, and others from Kumbheśvara Ṭola, Lalitpur, jointly installed brasspatāḥs (decorative metal leaves) on the temple.
